events.title: The excommunication of Elizabeth I
events.shortBlurb: By the bull Regnans in Excelsis Pope St. Pius V excommunicated the queen of England and deepened the trial of her Catholic subjects…
body: On 25 February 1570 Pius V published the bull Regnans in Excelsis ('He who reigns on high'). It pronounced 'Elizabeth, the pretended queen of England and the servant of crime' a heretic, excommunicated her, declared her deprived of her pretended right to the throne, and absolved her subjects from every oath of allegiance, threatening with the same sentence any who should obey her laws.

The blow came too late for its design: issued in belated support of the rising of the northern Catholic earls, it arrived after that rebellion had been crushed. In London John Felton boldly posted the bull on the gate of the Bishop of London's palace near St Paul's; he suffered death for it on 8 August 1570 and was later beatified among the martyrs of England.

Far from shaking the queen, the bull left every English Catholic a suspected traitor. Parliament answered it with the Treasons Act of 1571, and the Ridolfi plot of the same year hardened the government further; the penal statutes under which Edmund Campion and hundreds more suffered death followed. In 1580 Gregory XIII, at the plea of the Jesuit missioners, quietly suspended the force of the bull for Catholics in England.
